name: Ready Mix
root_cause_rev: Q1 revenue underperformance was primarily attributable to the rainy season, which traditionally represents a lean period for the construction materials industry, resulting in lower sales volume and reduced capacity utilization. Limited market penetration and the absence of an RMC plant within Dhaka City further constrained market access and increased logistics and distribution costs. Additionally, competitive pricing pressure, lower conversion of sales leads into confirmed orders, and challenges in acquiring new customers and retaining existing ones contributed to the shortfall against the budgeted revenue target.
root_cause_loss: The Q1 net loss resulted from inadequate revenue and volume absorption against a high fixed-cost base, low and fluctuating gross margins, high logistics and distribution expenses, manufacturing overhead, and substantial financial expenses. Lower capacity utilization and unfavorable selling-price-to-cost relationships further weakened profitability. The September deterioration in GP margin and the continuing negative EBIT demonstrate the need for immediate cost and margin correction.
plan_rev: Implement a focused, volume-driven revenue recovery strategy by strengthening key-account management, acquiring new customers, recovering lost orders, expanding market coverage in high-potential areas, and maximizing plant utilization. Ensure the realization of approved selling-price increases and eliminate unjustified lower prices for 3,000 PSI, 3,500 PSI, 4,000 PSI, and 4,500 PSI concrete grades. The key objectives are to achieve 100% of the approved monthly revenue budget, ensure sustainable sales volume growth, and progressively recover the Q1 revenue shortfall of Tk 25.77 Cr.
plan_loss: Execute a profitability-led turnaround focused on improving contribution per CFT, reducing material and logistics costs, increasing plant utilization, controlling overhead, and reducing financing costs through stronger receivables collection and working-capital management. Target positive monthly EBIT and EAT, sustainable gross-margin improvement, and achievement of at least the approved EAT budget. Eliminate the Q1 adverse EAT budget gap of Tk 8.38 Cr through validated incremental contribution and cost savings.

name: Commodities – F&B
root_cause_rev: Q1 FY26-27 net revenue BDT 3.09 Cr against a BDT 7.25 Cr budget — a shortfall of BDT 4.16 Cr (43% achievement): Jul 1.465 vs 1.62 (90%), Aug 0.543 vs 1.66 (33%), Sep 1.085 vs 3.97 (27%). The deficit is supply-driven, not demand-driven. The Malaysia and Thailand import lines that carry the core range were not opened in the quarter, so 56% of finished-goods SKUs (82 of 146) sat at zero stock and three new categories budgeted at BDT 1.64 Cr never traded. A customs branch lock on one Thailand shipment held ~BDT 2.18 Cr of sellable stock for most of July, and a C&F transition that was not F&B-ready produced clearance delays and misdeclared HS codes on 3 of 18 lines. Sell-in was further constrained by credit holds on the two customers who represent ~78% of revenue. Demand was intact — July hit 90% of budget and collections ran at 81% — the business simply had nothing to sell.
root_cause_loss: PAT −BDT 1.49 Cr against a budgeted profit of BDT 0.30 Cr — adverse BDT 1.79 Cr (Jul −0.357, Aug −0.866, Sep −0.264); EBITDA −1.09 Cr against +1.01 Cr budget. Most of the loss is non-recurring import shock: BDT 87L exceptional cost (BDT 37L demurrage and penalties on a held shipment, BDT 50L from a C&F assessment error that raised Gatorade from USD 1.50 to 7.92) plus a BDT 38.83L NRV write-down. The remainder is structural: volume at 43% of plan cannot absorb fixed cost — August COGS exceeded revenue — gross margin was negative to thin in July–August and only recovered in September.
plan_rev: Rebuild the range, then hold a steady BDT 2.50 Cr monthly run-rate. Supply is anchored on the approved 5-LC import plan of BDT 10.82 Cr landed (24,185 cartons, 157 SKUs), which carries 17.97% gross margin and 4.19% net margin and is already in execution under CEO approval. Alongside that, widen the channel so the run-rate is not dependent on two accounts: Modern Trade, HORECA, Akij Essential retail, sole distributorship of high-demand lines and demand-led local purchase. Target state: BDT 2.50 Cr/month sustained from November, ~95% availability on the top-20 SKUs, 60%+ of 69 accounts active against 14 today, top-2 customer concentration below 50%, blended GP 18%, and monthly PAT positive. FY27 revenue lands at ~BDT 24.70 Cr against the BDT 36.61 Cr ABP, which is re-baselined with the Board rather than left as an unachievable number.
plan_loss: Separate recurring trading margin from exceptional import cost, then price every SKU off true landed cost so a BDT 2.50 Cr run-rate produces a positive bottom line. At the approved import plan's 17.97% GP and 4.19% NP, BDT 2.50 Cr/month yields roughly BDT 0.10 Cr PAT per month. Target state: blended GP 18%, monthly PAT breakeven from November-26, Q3 and Q4 each contributing ~BDT 0.30 Cr, FY27 loss contained to ≤BDT 0.90 Cr against a −5.96 Cr annualized Q1 run-rate, DIO cut from 59 to 45 days, and the BDT 1.49 Cr Q1 loss recovered through trading margin and cost, not one-off gains.
owner_text: Md. Imran Hossen, Head of Sales – ACL (Imported Food Business), reporting to Md. Akterul Alam Shah, COO, Akij Essential.
target_date: 30-Nov-2026 for monthly PAT breakeven; 31-Mar-2027 for a sustained BDT 2.50 Cr run-rate and completion of the recovery plan.

name: LifeCare – Pharmacy
root_cause_rev: 1. Expansion was slower than budgeted. Outlet growth was deliberately slowed (34 outlets now), and new outlets take longer to reach maturity, so revenue from new stores lagged the budget. 2. The budget assumed a steeper ramp than the network delivered. Budget grew 36% from July to September (7.21 → 9.79). Actual sales grew 25% (6.19 → 7.77). The monthly gap widened from 1.02 to 1.29 to 2.02 Cr. Actual sales are growing; they are just growing more slowly than budget assumed. 3. Competitive pressure is high. Neighborhood pharmacies and online players (discount-led) are taking sales.
root_cause_loss: 1. GP is too thin to cover the cost base. GP of 11.9% (11.6% in September, falling) yields about 2.5 Cr per quarter against about 4.9 Cr of costs. 2. Fixed costs are high relative to current sales. Outlet rent, staff and head-office overhead were sized for the budgeted network and volume. Sales per outlet are only about 23 lakh a month. 3. The margin is being diluted. Customer discounts are given to compete, high-margin categories are a small share of sales, and supplier terms for trade discounts and bonuses are weak. 4. Working capital costs are rising. Mostly cash purchasing, inventory build-up, and some expiry or slow-moving stock add finance cost. Note: EAT came in 0.12 Cr better than budget, so cost control is working. The gap is structural, driven by revenue and margin.
plan_rev: Approach: grow same-store sales first, through repeat customers, bigger baskets and better mix, rather than new outlets. Use data and segmentation at outlet level. Add online sales as an extra channel. Target state: monthly net sales grow about 5% month on month, from 7.77 Cr (September) to 12.41 Cr by June 2027. Q2 (Oct–Dec) sales reach at least 25.5 Cr, which equals Q1’s budget and is 4.3 Cr above Q1 actual.
plan_loss: Approach: work on three levers together- 1. Raise GP% through mix, purchasing terms and discount discipline. 2. Hold the cost base flat while sales grow (operating leverage). 3. Cut working-capital and finance costs. Target state: 1. GP rises to about 13% by December and to 14% or more by June 2027. 2. Opex as a share of sales falls from about 23% to about 14%. 3. Q2 loss falls to 1.6 Cr or less. 4. Monthly EAT breaks even by June 2027.

Finance and the outlet-level P&L: Aynanul Hoque, FC People changes: Md. Arif Rahman, HRBP.
target_date: Interim milestones by 31 Dec 2026: credit purchasing in place, GP around 13%, Q2 targets met. Full recovery by 30 Jun 2027.

name: ABSL – Asphalt
root_cause_rev: The revenue shortfall was mainly caused by the rainy season, which reduced road construction activities and asphalt demand, and the unavailability of LC bitumen, forcing the company to purchase higher priced local bitumen. This weakened price competitiveness and reduced order conversion. Q1 revenue was Tk 7.62 Cr against a budget of Tk 30.65 Cr, resulting in a deficit of Tk 23.03 Cr (75.1%).
root_cause_loss: Low revenue and sales volume resulted in inadequate absorption of fixed costs. Higher priced local bitumen, Lower sales demand, and increased sales price weakened profitability. GP margin declined to -9.9% in September. Consequently, Q1 EAT was a loss of Tk 2.15 Cr against a budgeted profit of Tk 0.01 Cr, creating an adverse gap of Tk 2.16 Cr.
plan_rev: Ensure timely LC bitumen procurement, strengthen customer acquisition, recover lost orders, and expand market coverage among RHD, LGED, City Corporations, MES and other contractors and infrastructure projects. Improve price competitiveness and plant utilization to achieve 100% of the approved monthly revenue budget and progressively recover the Tk 23.03 Cr shortfall.
plan_loss: Improve contribution per MT through competitive bitumen procurement, better selling price realization and strict cost control. Optimize working capital to achieve positive monthly EBIT and EAT and recover the Tk 2.16 Cr adverse EAT budget gap.

name: Next JobZ
root_cause_rev: Q1 revenue = 91.7% of budget (0.62 Cr vs 0.68 Cr; −0.06 Cr; Jul 80.2% → Aug 95.0% → Sep 96.8%, Sep = 3.17M = 100.1% of budget). Root causes: (1) the 68.3%-planned Payroll/Staffing pillar was still in setup most of Q1 (DIFE license + payroll-disbursement infra; first staffing revenue only in Aug at ৳1.03M), so the quarter ran on a substitute mix of ~61% Training + ~33% LinkedIn resale; (2) 9 of 14 revenue streams stayed inactive (CV/Career Services, BGV, Salary Survey, Employer Branding, Assessment, CV Bank, International/Remote, RMS/ATS SaaS, Premium Subscription = ৳0); (3) employer accounts barely monetized — 7,343 accounts but only 636 verified and ~23–35 paid posts/mo; (4) weak demand conversion — 86% of 'active' flags expired, ~200–232 genuinely live jobs, no self-serve checkout / CRM / GA4 value events.
root_cause_loss: Q1 EAT = BDT −1.80 Cr (vs −2.92 Cr budget, favourable by 1.12 Cr, but worsening Jul→Sep). Root causes: (1) gross-margin collapse — GP% 96.8% (Jul) → 43.7% (Aug) → 1.5% (Sep); Q1 blended 36.7%; Sep's ~1.5% GP on 0.29 Cr revenue is the driver as mix shifted to low/zero-margin LinkedIn resale + one-off training while the high-margin payroll/staffing pillar was still ramping; (2) marketing overspend — Q1 ~BDT 16.19M vs ~10.11M budget (160%), S&M ~3.8× revenue; (3) broken unit economics — CAC ≈ ৳126,400 vs LTV ≈ ৳29,900 (LTV:CAC 0.24 vs 11.67× plan); (4) fixed cost base built ahead of revenue, with 9 of 14 streams inactive and the 68.3% pillar producing ~BDT 0 until Aug.
plan_rev: Pivot to a Payroll-Staffing-Training-led engine, amplify employer-account monetization, and convert the 9 inactive revenue streams to active. (1) Scale Payroll/Staffing/RPO (68.3% pillar) on 3 models — % of payroll disbursement (4–10%), per-head ৳600–1,200, prepaid per-position ৳500–700 (Model 3) — to ≥৳9.5L/mo (stretch ৳15L). (2) Rebuild Training (corporate + public + government) to ≥৳13L/mo. (3) Monetize the 7,343 employer accounts (636 verified → 1,000+) to ≥৳4L/mo and 300 paid posts/mo. (4) Activate ≥6 of 9 inactive streams (CV, BGV, Salary Survey, Employer Branding, Assessment, CV Bank, International, RMS/ATS, Premium) with first revenue. Target by Dec-26: 20–30L/mo exit run-rate, LTV:CAC 0.24 → ≥0.45, employer retention 18% → 40%, staffing-led high-GP mix.
plan_loss: Cash-first sequencing + gross-margin repair + spend discipline. (1) Protect working capital first: collections sprint, DSO 60→45 days, receivables 4.0M→≤2.2M, Group salary-float facility term sheet by 31 Oct. (2) Repair margin: shift mix to staffing (VAT on fee-only), pricing lock, commission redesign (2× staffing/posting/CV/BGV, 0.5× LinkedIn resale), cap LinkedIn ≤15% of mix. (3) Discipline spend: freeze paid jobseeker acquisition while LTV:CAC <1; tier-gated marketing. Target state: EAT loss ≤ budget and trending to breakeven; GP% restored toward 60%+; LTV:CAC ≥0.45 by Dec (path ≥1 by Jun-27).

name: Consumer Electronics
root_cause_rev: We are significantly behind our original expansion plan due to a shortage of funds and manpower. So far, we have successfully opened four showrooms, with another scheduled to open by 30 October 2026. The delay in showroom openings has negatively impacted business performance, resulting in a decline in sales. In addition, product availability has been severely affected due to zero stock at the principal level. Furthermore, our ability to procure and replenish the available products has been constrained by the ongoing funding shortage. These challenges have collectively hindered our planned business growth and expansion.
root_cause_loss: Net loss in Q1 was primarily driven by delayed showroom openings, resulting in lower-than-planned revenue, product shortages due to principal stock unavailability, and limited working capital to support inventory and business operations. High operating costs relative to sales further impacted profitability.
plan_rev: We are prioritizing fund availability by exploring bank financing options to address our current financial constraints. At the same time, we are accelerating showroom expansion and ensuring faster execution of the remaining expansion plans. Additionally, we are prioritizing the immediate recruitment of manpower to strengthen our Corporate Sales and HVAC businesses, while also expanding our Omni-channel operations to enhance market coverage, improve sales performance, and drive sustainable business growth.
plan_loss: Recover losses by accelerating showroom expansion, securing bank financing to ensure adequate product availability, and recruiting key manpower for Corporate Sales, HVAC, and Omni-channel operations. The target state is to achieve sustainable revenue growth, improve operational efficiency, optimize costs, and restore profitability.
